about: Chiata Foton is the entry for a Chinese company in Nanjing, Jiangsu, in automotive sales and service, probably a vehicle distribution business linked to the Foton commercial vehicle brand, which is part of Beiqi Foton. Recorded funding is about 354 million Chinese yuan. It is listed. Its exact role, ownership and scale are not confirmed here. B2B automotive dealer or service brand with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Saudi Automotive Services Company (SASCO) is a Saudi company, based in Riyadh, that provides vehicle-related services such as fuel station operations, car services and commercial vehicle and automotive sales and maintenance, with a large network of service stations in the Kingdom. It is listed on Tadawul. Recorded funding is about 190 million Saudi riyals. Consumers know the Sasco-branded fuel and service stations. Details of its current business mix and ownership are not fully confirmed here.

Ardmore Shipping is an Irish-managed (Cork) shipping company, listed on the NYSE (ASC), that owns and operates a fleet of about 25 modern product and chemical tankers, carrying refined petroleum products and chemicals for oil majors, traders and chemical companies. It earns revenue from vessel charters. It was established in 2010 and operates globally with offices in Cork, Singapore and the US. Recorded funding is shown as 25 million dollars. B2B shipping brand with no consumer awareness.

Greatland Electrics is a Shenzhen, Guangdong-based Chinese company, listed among public companies, whose industries are automotive and manufacturing. Recorded funding is about 244 million Chinese yuan. Its products, customers and listing venue are not confirmed here, though the sector suggests electrical components for vehicles supplied to manufacturers. Likely a B2B supplier with no known consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Parrot is a French drone and wireless technology company based in Paris, founded in 1994, known for consumer drones such as the AR.Drone and Bebop, and now focused on professional and defence drones including the Anafi family for inspection, public safety and military customers. Customers include the French and US armed forces. Revenue is about 50 million euros. It is listed on Euronext Paris (PARRO). Once a mass consumer brand in drones, now mainly B2B and defence.

PPM Solution is a Shenzhen, Guangdong-based Chinese company, listed among public companies, in the automotive and manufacturing industries. Recorded funding is about 224 million Chinese yuan. Its products, customers and listing venue are not confirmed here, though the sector suggests components or equipment supplied to vehicle makers. Likely a B2B supplier with no known consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Unifly is a Beijing-based Chinese company, listed among public companies, with Crunchbase industries in automotive and electric vehicles. Recorded funding is about 197 million Chinese yuan. Its products, customers, ownership and listing venue are not confirmed here. Likely an EV-related technology or components business, aimed at B2B customers, with no known consumer profile. Not to be confused with the Belgian drone traffic firm of the same name. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Whoosh is Russia's largest kick-scooter sharing operator, with a Cyprus-registered holding company, operating electric scooters and e-bikes through an app in around 40 Russian cities and in Kazakhstan, Belarus and Uzbekistan. Customers are urban riders who pay per minute. It listed on the Moscow Exchange (WUSH) in 2022. Recorded funding is about 25 million dollars. Subject to sanctions-related complications for Western partners. Recognised urban mobility brand within Russia.

NAVYA was a French maker of autonomous electric shuttles and driverless vehicles, based in Villeurbanne near Lyon and founded in 2014. Its Autonom Shuttle and Autonom Cab were used on campuses, airports and city pilots for public transport operators and industrial sites. It was listed on Euronext Growth Paris but ran into financial trouble and entered receivership in 2023, after which it was taken over by Gaussin Macnica Mobility. Crunchbase shows about 101 million in funding, latest in October 2022. Niche B2B brand, well covered in mobility press.

Creditas Financial is listed in the data as a Cayman Islands vehicle finance broker, linked to Creditas, the Sao Paulo secured-lending fintech that offers auto-backed loans, home equity loans and payroll loans in Brazil and Mexico. Creditas was founded in 2012, valued at about $4.8 billion in 2021, and raised funding totalling around $222M in the supplied record, most recently in 2022. Customers are consumers who borrow against assets. Notable fintech brand in Brazil with significant advertising.

about: Think Global, or Think, was a Norwegian electric car maker based in Fornebu near Oslo, best known for the small City electric vehicle. Founded as Pivco in the 1990s, it was owned at various times by Ford, then investors including Kleiner Perkins and Ener1, and produced cars in Norway and Finland. It filed for bankruptcy in 2011 after repeated funding problems, with funding of about $157M recorded by 2010. Defunct EV brand with historic profile, and no sponsorship activity today.

about: Kinaxis is an Ottawa software company, founded in 1984, whose RapidResponse platform provides supply chain planning, demand forecasting and scenario modelling for large manufacturers in sectors such as consumer goods, automotive, high tech and life sciences. Customers include Unilever, Ford, Subaru and Pfizer, and revenue is about US$500M mainly from subscriptions. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (KXS). B2B software brand known to supply chain executives, with some sports sponsorship in Canada.

about: iCar Asia operated online car marketplaces in Southeast Asia from Kuala Lumpur, including Carlist.my in Malaysia, Mobil123 in Indonesia and One2Car in Thailand, plus automotive classifieds and dealer advertising. It listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ICQ) and Bursa-related markets. Later ownership changes are not confirmed here. Funding of about $39M was recorded in 2017. Consumer automotive classified brands with strong recognition in Malaysia and Indonesia.

Rolex Rings is an Indian forging company based in Rajkot, Gujarat, making hot-forged and machined bearing rings and automotive components, supplied to makers of bearings, transmissions and equipment for global OEMs in Europe, the US and Asia. It listed on the NSE and BSE in 2021 (ROLEXRINGS). It has no connection to the Swiss watch maker. Customers are bearing and automotive firms, and revenue is around INR 11 billion. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer recognition.

about: Sandhar Technologies is an Indian automotive components maker based in Gurugram, producing locks, mirrors, handles, switches, lighting and sheet metal parts for two-wheeler, passenger car and commercial vehicle makers such as Hero, Honda, Mahindra and Maruti. It operates dozens of plants in India and abroad. It listed on the NSE and BSE in 2022 (SANDHAR). Funding of about $32M was recorded in 2014. B2B supplier with revenue near INR 35 billion and no consumer brand awareness.

about: Endurance Technologies is an Indian automotive component maker based in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra. It makes suspension systems, braking systems, transmission parts and aluminium die-cast components, mainly for two- and three-wheelers, with customers such as Bajaj Auto, Royal Enfield and Hero MotoCorp, plus European customers. Founded in 1985 and listed on NSE and BSE since 2016, it has annual revenue of more than 100 billion rupees. It is a B2B supplier with little consumer brand profile.

about: Honeywell Aerospace makes aircraft engines (auxiliary power units, turbofans), avionics, cockpit systems, braking, satellites and parts and services for commercial, defence and space customers. Revenue near 15 billion dollars. Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. A segment of Honeywell, which has planned to spin it off as a separate listed company in the second half of 2026. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Bombardier is a Canadian manufacturer of business jets, including the Challenger and Global families (Global 7500 and 8000), with servicing and defence modifications. Sells to wealthy individuals, corporates and governments, with revenue near 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Montreal, Quebec; founded 1942. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (BBD.B). It sold its rail business to Alstom in 2021 and aerospace commercial units earlier. Premium aviation brand with narrow audience.

FTAI Aviation owns and leases commercial aircraft engines and parts and runs an engine maintenance and parts business, serving airlines worldwide. Revenue near 2.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York; spun out of Fortress Transportation and Infrastructure Investors in 2022 (infrastructure assets went to a separate company). Listed on Nasdaq (FTAI). B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Rocket Companies is a US financial technology holding company, with Rocket Mortgage, Rocket Homes, Rocket Loans and Rocket Money, plus the acquired Redfin and Mr. Cooper. Provides online home loans, personal loans and personal finance tools to consumers. Revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Detroit, Michigan; founded by Dan Gilbert as Quicken Loans in 1985. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RKT). Strong US consumer brand, famous for its Super Bowl advertising and naming rights to Rocket Arena in Cleveland.

Qnity Electronics is a Wilmington, Delaware company spun out from DuPont in November 2025, supplying materials and technology for semiconductor manufacturing and advanced electronics, including CMP pads and slurries, photoresists and interconnect materials. Customers are chipmakers like TSMC, Samsung and Intel and electronics manufacturers worldwide, with annual revenue near $4 billion. Listed on NYSE (Q). B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

iSpace (Beijing Interstellar Glory Space Technology) is a Chinese commercial rocket company, founded in 2016 and based in Beijing, that builds the Hyperbola solid and liquid-fuel launch vehicles and reusable rockets for small satellite launches. Customers are satellite operators and government-linked users. It was among China's first private firms to reach orbit (2019). Reported funding is about $1.3 billion. B2B aerospace, little public brand awareness outside China.

about: Rolls-Royce Holdings is a London-based engineering company making civil and defence aerospace engines (Trent, Pearl, Adour), nuclear submarine reactors, small modular reactors and Power Systems (mtu engines, power generation). Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, the luxury car maker, is owned separately by BMW. Revenue is around 18 billion pounds. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (RR.). Customers are airlines, airframers, and governments. Strong global brand, with aerospace sponsorship and heritage.

United Launch Alliance (ULA) is a Centennial, Colorado-based rocket launch provider, a 50/50 joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin formed in 2006, flying Atlas V, Delta IV and the new Vulcan Centaur rockets for NASA, the US Space Force, the National Reconnaissance Office, and commercial customers including Amazon's Project Kuiper. B2B and government, with high profile in the space industry and some public awareness from launch broadcasts.

ARIDGE (Aridge, formerly part of Xpeng's flying car business) is a Chinese electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) and urban air mobility company, developing flying cars including the Land Aircraft Carrier, which carries a flying module. Based in Guangzhou, it is an XPENG spin-off and affiliate. Reported funding is about $950 million. Pre-commercial, aimed at consumers and tourism. Recognised in EV and tech media, with limited consumer brand awareness yet.

The input shows reported funding of about $955 million. Customers are US military and government. B2B and defense, with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Anduril Industries is a Costa Mesa, California defense technology company, founded in 2017 by Palmer Luckey, making autonomous systems, sensors and software such as Lattice, Ghost drones, Roadrunner interceptors and the Fury combat aircraft. Customers are the US Department of Defense and allied governments. It raised a total of about $11.4 billion and was valued at over $30 billion in 2025. B2B and government, with strong media profile but little consumer brand.

Rocket Lab is a Long Beach, California launch and space systems company, founded in New Zealand in 2006 by Peter Beck, flying Electron small rockets and developing the Neutron medium-lift vehicle, and building satellites and spacecraft components. Customers include NASA, the US Space Force and commercial satellite operators. Listed on Nasdaq (RKLB) after a 2021 SPAC. B2B and government, with high profile among space enthusiasts and investors.

TransDigm is a Cleveland, Ohio-based aerospace supplier (NYSE: TDG), owning proprietary components such as actuators, ignition systems, seating and cockpit controls for commercial and military aircraft. It grows by acquiring niche parts businesses and earns high margins on aftermarket spare parts, with revenue near $8 billion. Customers are Boeing, Airbus, airlines and the US military. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Air China is a Beijing-based Chinese flag carrier, a state-owned airline of the Air China Group, operating domestic and international passenger and cargo flights from hubs at Beijing Capital and Chengdu, with about 700 aircraft, and a member of the Star Alliance. Listed in Hong Kong, Shanghai and London (753, 601111). Controlled by China National Aviation Holding. Very high brand awareness in China, and an Olympic and sports partner.

Air France-KLM is a Paris-based airline group formed in 2004 by the merger of Air France and KLM, also owning Transavia and Martinair, with about 550 aircraft carrying around 100 million passengers a year. Listed on Euronext Paris and Amsterdam (AF), with the French state holding around 28 percent. Revenue is about 31 billion euros. Very high consumer brand awareness in Europe, and a sports and cultural sponsor.

Aircastle is a Stamford, Connecticut-based aircraft leasing company that acquires, leases and sells commercial jet aircraft to airlines worldwide, with a portfolio of about 250 aircraft. It is owned by Marubeni and Mizuho Leasing. Customers are airlines. B2B, no consumer brand awareness. Reported funding in the input is about $6 billion, mainly debt.

Archer Aviation is a San Jose, California electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) developer (NYSE: ACHR), building the Midnight air taxi for urban air mobility, with partners United Airlines, Stellantis and the UAE launch plan in Abu Dhabi. Founded in 2018, it listed via SPAC in 2021 and has raised billions of dollars. Pre-revenue. Customers are airlines and operators. Known among investors and aviation media, with the official air taxi role at the LA 2028 Olympics.

Aviation Capital Group is a Newport Beach, California-based aircraft leasing company, owned by Tokyo Century (Japan), with a portfolio of about 300 aircraft leased to airlines in more than 40 countries. It earns lease income. Reported funding is about $8.4 billion, mostly debt. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

AviLease is a Riyadh-based Saudi aircraft lessor owned by the Public Investment Fund, established in 2022, which buys and leases narrow- and wide-body aircraft to airlines and has placed large Airbus and Boeing orders. The input shows about $3.7 billion in funding. B2B aircraft leasing, with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Axon is a Scottsdale, Arizona-based public safety technology company (Nasdaq: AXON), maker of TASER conducted energy devices, body cameras, Evidence.com software and drones for law enforcement and military. Revenue is about $2.1 billion, with a subscription model. Customers are police departments and governments in over 100 countries. B2B, with the TASER name widely known in public.

Azul is a Sao Paulo-based Brazilian airline, founded in 2008 by David Neeleman, serving more than 150 destinations, mostly domestic, from its Campinas hub, with loyalty program TudoAzul. It carries about 30 million passengers a year and is listed on B3 and NYSE (AZUL). It filed for Chapter 11 in 2025. Consumers are Brazilian travellers. Strong consumer brand in Brazil, with football sponsorship.

Booz Allen Hamilton is a management and technology consulting firm headquartered in McLean, Virginia, founded in 1914 and listed on the NYSE (BAH). It sells consulting, cyber, analytics, AI and engineering services overwhelmingly to the US federal government, including defence, intelligence and civilian agencies, with roughly 35,000 employees and annual revenue above 11 billion dollars. Revenue comes from government contracts. Investment firm Carlyle was a long-time major shareholder before exiting. B2B and government contractor with modest public brand awareness outside Washington.

Dubai Aerospace Enterprise (DAE) is an aviation services company headquartered in Dubai, owned by the Investment Corporation of Dubai. It is one of the world's largest aircraft lessors (DAE Capital) with hundreds of aircraft, and also runs engineering and maintenance (DAE Engineering) and a regional MRO. Customers are airlines around the world; revenue comes from lease rentals and MRO services. Founded 2006. B2B aviation business with limited consumer awareness.

Eutelsat is a French satellite operator headquartered in Paris (Issy-les-Moulineaux), listed on Euronext Paris (ETL) and, following its 2023 merger with OneWeb, a provider of geostationary and low-earth-orbit connectivity. It sells broadcasting capacity to TV channels, broadband and mobility connectivity to governments, airlines, telcos and enterprises worldwide. The French state became its largest shareholder in a 2025 capital raise to support European sovereign satellite capacity. B2B infrastructure with modest public awareness.

Exchange Income Corporation (EIC) is a Winnipeg-based acquisition-oriented company listed on the TSX (EIF), with two segments: aerospace and aviation (regional airlines Perimeter, Calm Air, PAL Airlines, Canadian charters, aircraft maintenance and special mission aircraft) and manufacturing (Quest, Ben Machine, Water Services, Spartan Bioscience). It serves remote communities, governments and industry across Canada and abroad, with annual revenue above 2 billion Canadian dollars. Founded 2002. Regional airline brands, otherwise a B2B conglomerate.

IndiGo (InterGlobe Aviation) is India's largest airline by market share, with over 60 percent of domestic traffic and a fleet of 400 plus Airbus A320 family and ATR aircraft, flying to dozens of international destinations. Headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana, it was founded in 2006 and is listed on the NSE and BSE. It operates a low-cost model with ancillary revenue, and carries around 100 million passengers a year. Strong mass-market consumer brand in India and a large advertiser.

Joby Aviation is a US electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft developer headquartered in Santa Cruz, California, listed on the NYSE (JOBY). It is developing a five-seat piloted air taxi, with Toyota as a major investor and manufacturing partner, Delta Air Lines as a partner, and Uber links through its former Uber Elevate acquisition. It has begun flight tests and pursues FAA certification and launch in Dubai. Founded 2009 and pre-revenue. High-profile technology brand with strong media interest.

L3Harris Technologies is a major US defence and aerospace technology company headquartered in Melbourne, Florida, formed in 2019 from the merger of L3 Technologies and Harris Corporation, and listed on the NYSE (LHX). It builds communications, sensors, electronic warfare, space payloads and missile solutions for the Pentagon, allied governments and commercial space customers, with about 47,000 employees and revenue over 21 billion dollars. Revenue comes from government contracts. B2B defence supplier with limited consumer brand awareness.

Leonardo is an Italian aerospace, defence and security group headquartered in Rome, majority-owned by the Italian government's Ministry of Economy, and listed on Borsa Italiana (LDO). Formerly Finmeccanica, it makes helicopters (AgustaWestland), aircraft, electronics, cyber and space systems, with about 60,000 employees and revenue near 17 billion euros. Customers are militaries, governments and civil operators worldwide. B2B defence brand known in Italy and across industry; sponsorship interest mostly in technology and prestige.

Lockheed Martin is the world's largest defence contractor, headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland and listed on the NYSE (LMT). It builds the F-35 fighter, F-16, Black Hawk helicopters, missiles, missile defence and space systems, with about 120,000 employees and revenue near 70 billion dollars, predominantly from the US government and allied militaries. Formed in 1995 from Lockheed and Martin Marietta. B2B and government brand with high recognition but little consumer marketing; it is a known technology partner in motorsport-adjacent engineering.

Orbital Space Technology is a Beijing-based commercial aerospace company developing satellites and related space systems, including remote sensing small satellites and data services for commercial and government customers in China. The listed funding indicates significant private investment in China's commercial space sector. Operating status and revenue are not confirmed. B2B space company with low consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Rheinmetall is a German defence and automotive supplier headquartered in Dusseldorf, listed on the Frankfurt exchange (RHM) and a DAX member. It makes ammunition, armoured vehicles (Lynx, Boxer, Panther), air defence systems and military trucks for NATO armies, plus automotive parts. With about 30,000 employees, revenue passed 9 billion euros in 2024 and is rising on European rearmament. Founded 1889. It sponsors Borussia Dortmund, giving the brand visibility in European football and rising public awareness.

Shield AI is a defence technology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Diego, California, building the Hivemind AI pilot software and V-BAT and Nova drones that operate without GPS or communications. Customers are the US Department of Defense, special forces and allied militaries; revenue is contracts and software. It has raised several hundred million dollars at a valuation of several billion dollars. B2B defence brand known in the military and tech press, not a consumer brand.

Sirius XM is the US satellite and online audio entertainment company, headquartered in New York and listed on Nasdaq (SIRI). It sells subscriptions to music, talk and sports channels on SiriusXM, Pandora and Stitcher to roughly 33 million subscribers, mainly in cars, with revenue around 8.5 billion dollars. Liberty Media was its controlling shareholder until the 2024 merger of Liberty Sirius into SiriusXM. Founded 1990s. Strong US consumer brand with extensive sports and music programming, including NASCAR and NFL content.

StandardAero is a Scottsdale, Arizona aircraft engine maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) provider for business jets, helicopters, military and commercial aircraft, serving operators and engine makers like Honeywell, GE and Rolls-Royce. It has facilities across North America, Europe and Asia and about 7,000 employees, with revenue around 5 billion dollars. Owned by Carlyle until its NYSE listing (SARO) in October 2024. B2B aerospace services with limited public awareness.

Kaiser Aluminum is a US producer of semi-fabricated specialty aluminum products, headquartered in Franklin, Tennessee and listed on Nasdaq (KALU). It makes plate, sheet, extrusions and rod for aerospace, automotive, defence, general engineering and packaging customers from plants in the US and Canada, with revenue near 3 billion dollars. Founded 1946 by Henry J. Kaiser. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Samvardhana Motherson International (SAMIL) is the flagship company of India's Motherson Group, headquartered in Noida and listed on the NSE and BSE. It makes wiring harnesses, rear-view mirrors, plastic modules, bumpers and aerospace and medical components for car makers such as Volkswagen, Mercedes, BMW and Toyota, with 400 or so plants in about 40 countries and revenue over 1 trillion rupees. Founded 1975. B2B tier-one supplier with low consumer awareness.

Deutsche Lufthansa AG is Europe's largest airline group by revenue, with Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian, Brussels Airlines, Eurowings and ITA Airways, plus Lufthansa Technik and LSG catering. It flies about 120 million passengers a year, with revenue around 37 billion euros. Headquartered in Cologne, with hubs in Frankfurt and Munich (Crunchbase lists Frankfurt). Listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (LHA). Very strong global consumer brand, with a track record of sports partnerships.

ADQ is an Abu Dhabi sovereign investment and holding company, established in 2018, with a portfolio spanning food and agriculture (Agthia, Al Dahra), utilities (TAQA), healthcare, mobility and logistics (Etihad Rail, AD Ports Group), energy and real estate. Owned by the Abu Dhabi government, headquartered in Abu Dhabi, with assets of well over $200 billion. Investor and owner of many sponsor-capable companies. Low direct consumer visibility, though its holdings are better known.

Crane Company is a Stamford, Connecticut industrial technology company that makes engineered products for aerospace and electronics (Crane Aerospace & Electronics) and process flow technologies, including valves, pumps and payment and merchandising technologies, after a 2023 separation of Crane NXT. Customers are aircraft makers, defence, chemical, oil and gas and energy plants. Revenue is around $2 billion. Listed on NYSE (CR). B2B, low consumer brand awareness.

Embraer is a Brazilian aerospace manufacturer making E-Jets and E2 regional airliners, Phenom and Praetor business jets, the C-390 Millennium military transport and defence and security systems, plus services and eVTOL development through Eve. Headquartered in Sao Jose dos Campos, Brazil (the Saudi Arabia country tag looks wrong). Customers are airlines, governments and private jet owners, with revenue around $6 billion or more. Listed on B3 (EMBR3) and NYSE (ERJ). Well-known in aviation, with limited consumer visibility.

Northrop Grumman is a major US aerospace and defence contractor, building the B-21 Raider bomber, Sentinel ICBM, space systems, unmanned aircraft such as Global Hawk, missiles, cyber and mission systems. Customers are mainly the US Department of Defense and allied governments, with annual sales of about $40 billion and about 95,000 employees. Headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia. Listed on NYSE (NOC). Defence brand well known in government and aerospace, with limited consumer relevance and sensitive for sponsorship.

Coherent Corp., formerly II-VI Incorporated, makes engineered materials, lasers and optical networking components, including silicon carbide wafers and devices, datacom transceivers for AI data centres, and industrial and medical lasers. Customers are telecom and data centre operators, industrial and semiconductor manufacturers, with revenue of about $5 billion. Headquartered in Saxonburg, Pennsylvania. Listed on NYSE (COHR). B2B photonics supplier with little consumer visibility.

Aura Aero is a French aircraft manufacturer based at Toulouse-Francazal, developing the ERA regional hybrid-electric aircraft, the Integral R and E sport and training planes and electric aircraft concepts, with orders from airlines and flying clubs. Founded in 2018 by Jeremy Caussade and Wilfried Dubourg. Has raised about $592 million in total funding. Private. Emerging aerospace brand known in aviation circles, with limited general consumer awareness.

Avolon is a Dublin-based aircraft leasing company with a portfolio of over 1,000 owned, managed and on-order aircraft leased to airlines across the world, and one of the largest lessors. Founded in 2010 by former RBS aviation executives, it is owned by Bohai Leasing and ORIX, and not listed. Revenue comes from lease rentals, and its financing includes large debt facilities. B2B brand known in aviation finance, with no consumer awareness.

SMBC Aviation Capital is a Dublin-based aircraft leasing company, owning and managing a fleet of about 700 aircraft that it leases to airlines worldwide, with revenue from lease rentals. It is owned by Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Sumitomo Corporation and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation. Not listed. Large lessor within the aviation industry, with visibility to airlines but no consumer awareness.

AAR Corp is an aerospace and defence services company providing aviation aftermarket support: aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul, parts supply, expeditionary services and fleet management for commercial airlines and the US government. Headquartered in Wood Dale, Illinois, founded in 1951, with revenue of about $2.5 billion. Listed on NYSE (AIR). B2B brand known in aviation, with no consumer awareness.

Astranis builds small, dedicated geostationary communications satellites (MicroGEO) that give countries and telecom operators a faster, cheaper route to broadband coverage, with customers including Thaicom, Orbits Corp, Pacific Dataport and Anuvu. Headquartered in San Francisco and founded in 2015. Revenue comes from satellite sales and service. Has raised about $1.7 billion in funding. Private. B2B space brand with a strong profile in the satellite industry and little consumer awareness.

Beta Technologies builds electric aircraft: the ALIA CX300 conventional takeoff and landing plane and the ALIA VTOL vertical lift aircraft, along with electric propulsion systems and a network of aircraft chargers. Customers include cargo operators such as UPS, Bristow and Air New Zealand, and the US Air Force. Headquartered in South Burlington, Vermont, founded in 2017 by Kyle Clark. Listed on NYSE (BETA) after a 2025 IPO. B2B aerospace brand, known in the eVTOL sector.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (ASUR) operates nine airports in southeastern Mexico including Cancun, the busiest, plus Merida, Cozumel and Villahermosa, and airports in Puerto Rico (San Juan) and Colombia (Rionegro). Revenue comes from airport charges, retail and advertising, with about 50 million passengers a year. Listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (ASUR) and NYSE (ASR), with Grupo ADO a key shareholder. Notable advertising and partnership inventory through tourism traffic.

Hadrian builds AI-powered automated factories that make precision parts for aerospace and defence companies, aiming to speed production and cut cost for customers and the US government. Headquartered in Los Angeles area, with a large factory in Arizona. Founded in 2023 by Chris Power. Crunchbase shows about $2.3 billion in funding as listed. Private. B2B industrial technology brand, known in defence-tech investing.

Howmet Aerospace makes engineered products for aircraft and industrial gas turbines: jet engine airfoils and components, fasteners, forged wheels and structures, supplying Boeing, Airbus, GE Aerospace, RTX and Safran. Headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with revenue of around $7 billion. Formed in 2020 when Arconic split into Howmet and Arconic Corporation. Listed on NYSE (HWM). B2B aerospace supplier with no consumer awareness.

Karman Space & Defense makes mission-critical subsystems and components for missiles, space launch, hypersonics and defence platforms, supplying the US Department of Defense and prime contractors such as Lockheed Martin, RTX and Northrop Grumman. Headquartered in Huntington Beach, California. Listed on NYSE (KRMN) since its February 2025 IPO, with TCI Fund Management a major shareholder. B2B defence supplier, with no consumer awareness.

Kratos Defense & Security Solutions develops unmanned aerial systems such as the Valkyrie and target drones, hypersonic test systems, satellite ground systems, microwave electronics and cyber and training solutions for the US Department of Defense and allied governments. Headquartered in San Diego, California, with revenue of about $1.1 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (KTOS). B2B defence brand, with no consumer awareness and a sensitive category for sponsorship.

Lyntia Networks is a Spanish neutral wholesale fibre-optic and telecom infrastructure operator based in Alcobendas, Madrid, offering dark fibre, backhaul and connectivity services to telecom operators. Customers are carriers and large network users. Crunchbase shows about $1.8 billion in funding, including infrastructure investor capital and debt. Private. B2B infrastructure brand, with no consumer awareness.

about: MDA Space is a Canadian space technology company best known for building the Canadarm robotic arms used on the Space Shuttle and International Space Station, and now making satellites, antennae, robotics and Earth observation systems, including constellations for Telesat and Globalstar. Headquartered in Brampton, Ontario. Customers include governments and satellite operators. Listed on the TSX (MDA) since 2021. B2B brand, notable in the space sector.

Gilching-based German drone maker, founded 2015 near Munich, producing Vector, Twister and Trinity eVTOL unmanned aircraft for defence, mapping and agriculture. Customers are armed forces including Ukraine and Germany, as well as commercial surveyors. Valued about EUR 3 billion after 2025 funding led by Thiel and Balderton. B2B and defence brand with little consumer awareness. It has about 600 employees and production sites in Germany, with drones flying with the German armed forces.

Kent, Washington, space start-up founded in 2020 by former Blue Origin engineers, developing the Nova fully reusable two-stage launch vehicle and a reusable upper stage. Customers would be satellite operators and government agencies. Funding shown is about $2.4 billion. Privately held. Space-industry brand with niche awareness and no existing consumer profile. The company is based near Seattle, has several hundred employees and tests its engine hardware at its facilities in Washington state.

Ottawa-based Canadian satellite operator, founded 1969, providing geostationary satellite connectivity to broadcasters, telecoms, airlines and governments, and building the Telesat Lightspeed low-earth-orbit network. Revenue is about CAD 0.9 billion. Listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (TSAT). B2B space infrastructure with no consumer awareness. Operates a satellite fleet. Telesat employs roughly 400 people and is building its Lightspeed constellation with MDA, supported by Canadian government funding.

Commercial spaceline founded by Richard Branson's Virgin Group, headquartered in California and operating from Spaceport America in New Mexico, flying paying customers on suborbital spaceplanes and developing next-generation Delta ships. Revenue is small. Listed on the NYSE (SPCE). Strong consumer brand name via Virgin, though flights have been few. The company has a few hundred employees and sells tickets at roughly $450,000 each for a short suborbital flight.

Dubai-based private aviation holding company, parent of VistaJet and XO, founded by Thomas Flohr, offering membership jet cards, charter and fleet services to wealthy individuals and corporates globally. Funding shown is about $2 billion. Privately held. Luxury aviation brand with high visibility among wealthy travellers and a record in sports sponsorships. Its services also include aircraft sales and fractional ownership, and the group has a combined fleet of hundreds of jets.

Yuanxin Satellite is a Shanghai-based provider of low-orbit broadband and multimedia satellite services in China, in the information and communications sector. The input shows funding of about 13.7 billion yuan. Likely state-linked B2B and government customers, with no consumer visibility. The input lists it in information and communications, but customer names, ownership and satellites are not given. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Paris-area defence, aerospace, security and digital identity group, founded in 1893 as Thomson-CSF, with revenue around EUR 20 billion and about 80,000 employees. Customers are armed forces, governments, airlines and enterprises (including cybersecurity and Gemalto SIM cards). Owned about a quarter each by the French state and Dassault; listed on Euronext Paris (HO). B2B brand. Thales employs around 80,000 people and operates in more than 60 countries, and also supplies avionics and satellites.

Polaris Inc. is a US manufacturer of powersports vehicles: off-road vehicles (RZR, Ranger, General), snowmobiles, Indian Motorcycle, Slingshot three-wheelers, Polaris boats and defence vehicles through Polaris Government and Defense. Sales are about 7 billion dollars annually and customers are consumers, dealers and military buyers, sold in North America and overseas. Founded in 1954 in Roseau, Minnesota, headquartered in Medina, Minnesota (Crunchbase shows Ohio) and listed on the NYSE (PII). Strong consumer brand in motorsports and outdoor recreation, with a long history of racing sponsorships.

about: SES is a Luxembourg-based satellite operator, with headquarters at Betzdorf, running geostationary and medium-earth-orbit (O3b mPOWER) fleets used for video broadcasting, data connectivity, mobility and government services. Customers include broadcasters, telecoms operators, cruise lines, airlines and defence agencies. Listed on Euronext Paris and Luxembourg (SESG), it completed the acquisition of Intelsat in 2025. Revenue is about 2 billion euros. B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

Air Canada is Canada's largest airline and flag carrier, based in Montreal, with a global network of 200 destinations, operating mainline and regional services plus the Aeroplan loyalty programme and Air Canada Rouge. It is a Star Alliance member, listed on the TSX (AC), with about 40,000 employees and revenue over 20 billion Canadian dollars. Customers are leisure and business travellers worldwide. Very high consumer visibility in Canada, and a long-standing sponsor of sports and events including the Olympics.

General Electric is the US industrial conglomerate founded by Thomas Edison in 1892, which split in 2023 to 2024 into GE Aerospace, making jet engines (with CFM International), GE HealthCare and GE Vernova, making power and wind equipment. The Crunchbase entry shows Boston as headquarters, the group's base from 2016 until the split. Customers are airlines, utilities, hospitals and governments. GE Aerospace is listed on the NYSE (GE). Hugely recognised brand worldwide, with some history in sports sponsorship.

AeroVironment is a US defence and aerospace technology company, based in Arlington, Virginia, known for small unmanned aircraft systems such as the Raven, Puma, Switchblade loitering munition and Jump 20, plus electric vehicle chargers earlier. Customers are the US Department of Defense and allied militaries. Founded in 1971 by Paul MacCready, it is listed on Nasdaq (AVAV) and acquired BlueHalo in 2025. Revenue is over 1 billion dollars. B2B government supplier with limited consumer awareness.

GE Aerospace is the independent jet and turboprop engine maker that emerged in April 2024 when General Electric completed the spin-off of GE Vernova, after earlier splitting off GE HealthCare. Based in Evendale near Cincinnati, Ohio, it makes engines through GE and its CFM joint venture with Safran for aircraft like the Boeing 737 and Airbus A320, plus defence engines and services. Listed on the NYSE (GE), with revenue of about 40 billion dollars. B2B brand with strong aviation visibility.

Phoenix Aviation Capital is a Stamford, Connecticut-based aircraft lessor, part of the Phoenix group, providing leased commercial aircraft and engines to airlines. Funding shown is about 2.4 billion dollars, probably credit facilities. B2B aviation finance with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Triumph Group is a US aerospace company, based in Radnor, Pennsylvania, manufacturing and servicing aircraft structures, systems and components, such as landing gear, actuation and hydraulics, for Boeing, Airbus, Gulfstream and military customers. It has operated in aerospace structures and aftermarket services. Listed on the NYSE (TGI) and agreed in 2025 to be acquired by Warburg Pincus and Berkshire Partners, taking it private. B2B supplier with no consumer awareness.

Bharat Forge is an Indian engineering company, part of the Kalyani Group, based in Pune, that makes forged and machined components for cars, trucks, aerospace, energy and defence, and is one of the world's largest forging firms. It has plants in India, Germany, the US, Sweden and elsewhere. Listed on the NSE and BSE (BHARATFORG), with revenue of over 150 billion rupees. B2B supplier with limited consumer awareness, though it supports Indian defence and motorsport links.

CDB Aviation is a Dublin-based aircraft leasing company and wholly owned subsidiary of China Development Bank Financial Leasing (CDB Leasing). It owns and leases commercial passenger aircraft to airlines worldwide, with a portfolio of several hundred aircraft, and earns lease rental income. Funding shown is about $2.6 billion. Customers are airlines, not consumers. B2B financial and aviation asset business with low public brand awareness.

ICEYE is a Finnish space technology company in Espoo, founded in 2014, that operates the world's largest constellation of small radar (SAR) imaging satellites, which can see through clouds and at night. It sells imagery and analytics to defence ministries, insurers, disaster response agencies and commercial users, with growing defence demand in Europe. It has raised over $2 billion in funding and is valued at over a billion dollars. B2B and government customers, with low consumer awareness.

Castelion is a Torrance, California defence technology startup, founded in 2022 and backed by investors including Lightspeed, that develops hypersonic weapons for the US military, notably the Blackbeard missile for the Army. It sells to the Department of Defense and has raised about $1.5 billion. Its team has many ex-SpaceX engineers. B2B and government customer, with limited public awareness and few consumer-facing marketing needs.

about: Dassault Systemes is a French software company based in Velizy-Villacoublay, listed on Euronext Paris (DSY), which sells 3D design, simulation and product lifecycle management software, including CATIA, SOLIDWORKS, SIMULIA and the 3DEXPERIENCE platform. Customers are industrial manufacturers in aerospace, automotive, life sciences and consumer goods, with revenue of about 6 billion euros. It is a long-standing technology partner in motorsport engineering. B2B, with high awareness among engineers but little among the general public.

Firefly Aerospace is a Cedar Park, Texas space company, founded in 2017, that builds small and medium launch vehicles (Alpha), the Blue Ghost lunar lander, which landed on the Moon in March 2025, and Elytra orbital vehicles. Customers are NASA, the US Space Force and commercial satellite companies. It listed on Nasdaq (FLY) in August 2025. Funding is about $1.4 billion. B2B and government, with strong awareness in space and engineering circles.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) is a Guadalajara-based airport operator with concessions for 12 airports in Mexico's Pacific region, including Guadalajara, Tijuana, Los Cabos and Puerto Vallarta, as well as airports in Jamaica (Montego Bay) and Costa Rica. It earns airport fees from airlines and retail and parking revenue. Listed in Mexico (GAP) and on the New York Stock Exchange (PAC). Travellers recognise its airports, though the company is B2B.

HEICO is a Hollywood, Florida aerospace, defence and electronics company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HEI), known for FAA-approved replacement parts for aircraft engines and airframes, which airlines use as a lower-cost alternative to original equipment. It also makes electronic and defence components, with revenue of about $4 billion and a strong acquisitive record. B2B, with high profile among aviation investors but little consumer awareness.

Hexcel is a Stamford, Connecticut advanced composites company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HXL), that makes carbon fibre, prepregs and honeycomb materials used in aircraft such as the Airbus A350 and Boeing 787, as well as defence, wind energy and motorsport applications. Revenue is about $1.9 billion. Customers are aircraft makers and tier suppliers. B2B, known in aerospace and racing engineering, with little consumer recognition.

Impulse Space is a Redondo Beach, California company, founded in 2021 by Tom Mueller, a SpaceX founding engineer, which builds orbital transfer vehicles and propulsion, such as Mira and Helios, to move satellites from launch drop-off to their final orbits and to Mars. It sells to commercial and government customers and has raised about $330 million per the input, with larger rounds publicly known. B2B space company, known in the aerospace community.

about: Isar Aerospace is a German launch company in Ottobrunn near Munich, founded in 2018, developing the Spectrum two-stage rocket to put small and medium satellites in orbit from Andoya, Norway. Its first launch attempt in March 2025 ended in failure after about 30 seconds of flight. It has raised more than $1 billion including funding from Eldridge and the European Investment Bank. B2B, building profile in European space.

Redwire is a Jacksonville, Florida space infrastructure company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RDW), which makes solar arrays, deployable structures, sensors and in-space manufacturing systems, and acquired Edge Autonomy in 2025. Customers include NASA, the US Space Force, Airbus and commercial satellite builders. Revenue is a few hundred million dollars. B2B, known in the space sector, with little consumer awareness.

Vertical Aerospace is a Bristol, UK aerospace company, founded in 2016 by Stephen Fitzpatrick, the founder of Ovo Energy, developing the VX4, a battery-electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft for air taxi use. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (EVTL), has raised well over a billion dollars and aims at certification in the UK and EU. Pre-revenue, with agreements from airlines such as American and Virgin Atlantic. Some brand visibility in aerospace.

Voyager Technologies is a Denver, Colorado defence and space technology company that provides satellite, propulsion, defence electronics and commercial space station services, including its work on the Starlab commercial space station with Airbus. It listed on the New York Stock Exchange (VOYG) in June 2025. Customers are NASA, the US Department of Defense and commercial space clients. B2B with a growing but niche profile.

Vulcan Elements is a Cambridge, Massachusetts manufacturer of rare-earth permanent magnets, founded in 2021, that builds US domestic magnet production to reduce dependence on China, selling to aerospace, defence, EV and industrial customers. It secured a large US government and Department of Defense backed financing in 2025. Recorded funding is about $1.17 billion. B2B supplier with little consumer visibility.

about: Airbus is the European aerospace and defence manufacturer, legally based in Leiden, Netherlands with main operations in Toulouse, Hamburg and Seville. It builds the A320, A350 and A380 airliners, H-series helicopters, military aircraft and satellites, with revenue of about 69 billion euros and 150,000 employees. Customers are airlines, lessors and governments. Listed on Euronext Paris (AIR). Recognised worldwide and a prolific sponsor, including of sport and events.

Axiom Space is a Houston, Texas space company, founded in 2016, that runs private astronaut missions to the International Space Station, builds commercial space station modules and develops next-generation spacesuits for NASA's Artemis programme. Customers are NASA, governments and private individuals. It has raised about $1 billion. B2B and government-facing, with high media profile in the space sector.

CesiumAstro is an Austin, Texas company, founded in 2017, that builds active phased array communications payloads and terminals for satellites, aircraft and drones. It sells to defence, space and commercial customers and has raised about $965 million per the input, though public rounds were lower. B2B with limited awareness outside aerospace and defence.

Chang Guang Satellite Technology is a Chinese commercial remote-sensing satellite company in Changchun, Jilin, spun out of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, operating the Jilin-1 satellite constellation that supplies imagery to agriculture, forestry, mapping and government customers. Funding shown is about CNY 7.7 billion. It has been the subject of US sanctions concerns. B2B and government-focused, with little consumer awareness.

Eve Air Mobility is a Melbourne, Florida urban air mobility company, a majority-owned subsidiary of Embraer, developing an electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) air taxi, and related services and air traffic software. It listed on the New York Stock Exchange (EVEX) in 2022 through a SPAC. It has pre-orders from airlines and lessors for hundreds of aircraft. Pre-revenue, with visibility in aerospace.

Falcata is an Arlington, Virginia defence technology company providing engineering and systems for defence customers, with recorded funding of about $1 billion. The Crunchbase text is limited and the company is not clearly known to us, so its scale, products and ownership should be checked. Likely a B2B and government supplier with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: GA Telesis is a Fort Lauderdale, Florida commercial aviation company, founded in 1996, that provides aircraft engine and component leasing, parts distribution, maintenance and aircraft teardown. It sells to airlines and lessors around the world, and has raised funding of about $925 million. B2B with low public brand awareness.

K2 Space is a Los Angeles company, founded in 2022 by former SpaceX engineers, which builds large, high-power satellite platforms (Mission-class and Gravitas) designed for launch on Starship and other rockets. It sells to government and commercial constellation operators and has raised about $925 million per the input, including rounds in 2025. B2B with limited public profile.

about: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) is a Mumbai-based Indian engineering and construction conglomerate, listed on the NSE and BSE, that builds infrastructure, power plants, buildings, hydrocarbon projects, defence equipment and IT services (LTIMindtree). Revenue is above 2 trillion rupees, with about 400,000 employees. A major national industrial brand, well known in India, and it sponsors some sporting events.

Mach Industries is a Huntington Beach, California defence manufacturer, founded in 2023 by Ethan Thornton, which builds autonomous drones and munitions, such as the Viper Strike glide weapon. It sells to US and allied defence customers and reportedly raised $100 million in 2025 and more, with funding of about $1.08 billion per the input. B2B and defence-focused, with limited awareness.

about: Planet Labs is a San Francisco aerospace and data analytics company, founded in 2010, which operates the largest fleet of Earth imaging satellites (Dove and SkySat) and sells daily imagery and analytics subscriptions to governments, agriculture, finance and defence customers. It listed on the New York Stock Exchange (PL) via SPAC in 2021. Funding shown is about $1.1 billion. B2B with a visible profile in the space sector.

True Anomaly is an Englewood, Colorado space security company, founded in 2022 by former US Space Force officers, which builds Jackal autonomous orbital vehicles for space domain awareness and rendezvous and proximity operations. Customers are the US Space Force and allied governments. It has raised about $1.05 billion. B2B and defence-focused, with limited public profile.

DISH Network is a Colorado pay-TV and wireless company with DISH satellite TV, Sling TV streaming and Boost Mobile, founded by Charlie Ergen. Customers are US households and mobile subscribers. EchoStar and DISH completed their merger at the end of 2023, so DISH is now a subsidiary of EchoStar (SATS), based in Englewood. Revenue about $15 billion. Strong consumer brands with past sports sponsorship and broadcast rights history.

We Energies is the trade name of Wisconsin Electric Power Company, a Milwaukee-based utility and subsidiary of WEC Energy Group (NYSE: WEC), providing electricity and natural gas to about 1.1 million electric and 1.1 million gas customers in Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula. Regulated rates are its revenue. Consumer-facing utility brand in Wisconsin and sponsor of community events and Milwaukee sports venues.

Aena is the Spanish state-controlled airport operator, headquartered in Madrid, managing 46 airports in Spain and stakes in airports abroad such as London Luton and Brazil, and handling over 300 million passengers a year. Revenue comes from airport charges and retail. Majority owned by ENAIRE (the state), listed on Spain's stock exchange (AENA). Well-known infrastructure brand in Spain, with large passenger reach.

Air India is India's flag carrier, based in Gurugram, Haryana, operating domestic and international flights; it was founded by JRD Tata in 1932, nationalised, and returned to the Tata Group in 2022, then merged with Vistara in 2024 and with AirAsia India, and it has placed one of the largest aircraft orders in history. Strong consumer brand across India and the diaspora, with sports sponsorship history.
